overview.description: Perudo (also known as Liar's Dice when played with dice) is a world-famous game of bluffing, probability, and nerve. This card-based adaptation replaces the dice cups with hidden hands of cards. Players must guess how many cards of a certain rank (e.g., 'Five Kings') are held collectively by everyone at the table. It is a game of extreme deception where you can win with the worst hand if you can successfully convince others you have the best.

history.origins: Rooted in the ancient game 'Dudo' from South America (Inca Empire), popularized globally as Perudo by Richard Blom in the 1980s. The card variant emerged as a portable alternative for those without dice sets.
timeline: 16th Century: Conquistadors observe 'Dudo' being played in Peru.
1987: Cosmobi toys releases Perudo as a commercial dice game.
2000s: Standardized card rules emerge for players using standard decks in pubs.
Present: A definitive 'Social Deception' game played in many cultures under different regional names.
history.evolution: The transition to cards adds a 'Non-Replacement' element to the probabilityâ€”if you hold 3 Kings, there are only 13 left in the entire deck, making the math more 'Concrete' than dice.
history.cultural: Famously associated with pirates (featured in 'Pirates of the Caribbean') and high-stakes social gambling.

setup.dealing: Each player is dealt 5 cards face-down. Do NOT show them to anyone.

rules.objective: Be the last player remaining with cards in your hand.
rules.gameplay: Each player is dealt 5 cards face-down and keeps them hidden. Play proceeds clockwise. On your turn you either make a bid or call Dudo. A bid states a quantity and a rank (e.g. Five Kings), meaning you believe that many cards of that rank (Aces often count as wild) exist across all players' hands. Each new bid must be higher: either a greater quantity or the same quantity of a higher rank. If you call Dudo you challenge the last bid; everyone reveals their hands. If the bid is correct the bidder wins the round and the challenger loses one card; if wrong the challenger wins and the bidder loses one card. The last player left with at least one card wins.
keyRules: Deal 5 cards each, all face-down and hidden.
Bid a quantity and rank (e.g. Three 7s); each bid must be higher quantity or same quantity higher rank.
Aces are usually wild and count as the bid rank.
Call Dudo to challenge; all reveal; loser of the challenge discards one card.

strategy.basic: Trust the math! With a 52-card deck and 5 players (25 cards total), the 'Average' amount of any one rank plus wilds is about 3. If someone bids 'Five 9s', they are likely bluffing unless they hold two 9s themselves. Always check your own hand first; if you have zero Jacks, your opponent's bid of 'Four Jacks' is high-risk.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Corner' Play: If you have a horrible hand (no pairs, no Aces), you MUST bluff early to push the bid up highly enough that the next player feels forced to call Dudo on the NEXT person. Bid small on a rank you don't have to 'Seed' the idea that you are strong, then Dudo your opponent when they try to overreach.
strategy.advanced: Joker-Ace Tracking: Keep track of how many Aces (wilds) have been discarded from the hands of eliminated players. If 3 Aces are gone, the 'Float' of the game drops significantly. A bid of 'Five Kings' becomes almost impossible without those wilds. The late-game is purely about card-counting the remaining deck potential.
tips: Keep a 'Poker Face'. In the card version, people will watch your eyes as you look at your hand more than in the dice version.
If you are the last player with 5 cards and your opponent has 1, you can take more risksâ€”but a 'Calza' can bring them back into the game.

difficulty.easy: Bids based only on its own hand; calls Dudo too often; doesn't count Aces.
difficulty.medium: Reasonable probability calculation; bluffs occasionally; manages the 'Calza' risk.
difficulty.hard: Expert at 'Bayesian Bluffing'; perfectly tracks remaining cards in the deck; analyzes betting patterns of opponents to detect lies.

bid.description: Claim a quantity and rank (e.g. Five Kings) that you believe exist across all players' hands combined. Aces count as wild for the bid rank. Each new bid must be higher quantity or the same quantity of a higher rank.
bid.constraints: Must be higher than the previous bid: either more cards or same count with a higher rank.

customActions.description: Challenge the previous bid. All hands are revealed; if the bid is correct the bidder wins the round and you lose one card; if wrong you win and the bidder loses one card.
customActions.constraints: Only legal when there is a previous bid to challenge.

engine.handRankingSystem: Not applicable; winner is last player with cards; no hand comparison.
engine.deckDescription: A standard 52-card French deck; the game may use cards for bidding or as a prop in a bluffing variant. Perudo-style bluffing involves claiming quantities or values; the deck provides the ranking or draw if used.
engine.suitDescription: The four French suits (hearts, diamonds, clubs, spades) with thirteen ranks each. In card-based Perudo bluff variants, suit may be irrelevant or used for wilds; the focus is on bluffing and calling.
engine.rankDescription: Standard ranks Ace through King; in bluffing games rank often represents a value or bid level. Players claim or challenge; the deck defines the possible values and the outcome of challenges.
